format.note: 18 clubs; our row is the Clausura. The season champion comes from a two-legged four-team play-off (Apertura winner, Clausura winner, best two of the aggregate table), not from the Clausura table. A club that wins both tournaments or tops the aggregate takes a bye, as Alianza Lima did in 2026.

playoff.entries: Apertura winner, Clausura winner, best two of the aggregate table
playoff.note: 2026 was reduced to one semi-final because Alianza Lima won the Apertura and led the aggregate; the final is two legs

stages: regional stage: 2 geographical groups of 9, double round-robin, 18 rounds
championship groups: 3 groups of 4, 6 rounds, with bonus points
format.note: the two regional group winners and the best runner-up start the championship groups on +2, the other runner-up and the third-placed clubs on +1

playoff.entries: top six of each regional group
playoff.note: semi-finals over two legs (three group winners plus best runner-up), final for the title and a repechaje for the losers; the champion goes up and the repechaje winner meets the final loser in a single match for the second promotion place

stages: Torneo Regional: 4 geographical groups of unequal size
quarter-finals, semi-finals and final over two legs
format.note: 37 clubs, eight of them reserve sides of Liga 1/2 clubs; the two finalists are promoted

playoff.note: quarter-finals, semi-finals and final over two legs; both finalists go up to Liga 2

boundaries.note: Liga 2 promotes through its play-offs: the champion (final winner) and the winner of a single runner-up match. Liga 1 relegates the bottom two of the season aggregate table (17th and 18th in 2025); a club can also lose its place administratively, as Binacional did in 2025.

Liga 3 promotes its two finalists, both via the knockout stage. Liga 2 relegates the bottom club of each of its two triangular relegation groups, so it is a group position rather than a division-wide bottom-n.

notes: Sizes 18/18/37 and levels 1/2/3 all match our rows. Liga 1 runs Apertura and Clausura of 17 rounds each plus an aggregate table; the season champion is decided by a four-team two-legged play-off, so the Clausura table alone does not crown anyone. Liga 2 has 18 clubs in two regional groups of 9 (18 rounds), three championship groups of 4 with bonus points, two triangular relegation groups of 3 (bottom club of each relegated) and a promotion play-off that sends the champion plus the runner-up-match winner up. Liga 3 is a 37-club competition in four unequal regional groups, then four groups of 4, then a two-legged knockout; eight of the clubs are reserve sides ('II') and reserve status is not a promotion bar (Sport Huancayo II went up for 2026). Liga 3's entry is not purely sporting: Copa Perú and U18 tournament promotions, withdrawals, mergers, exclusions and disqualifications reshape the field every season, so a seeded 37-team table will be wrong at the start of the season. Liga 3 relegates to the Copa Perú, which is not modelled.
